name: data-file-viewer
description: Open and explore .duckdb, .parquet, .csv, .dta (Stata), .arrow/.arrows/.feather (Arrow IPC), .xlsx (Excel), .db/.sqlite (SQLite), and kdb+ data files right inside VS Code, without needing a separate database program. A sidebar lists every table in the file — click one to see its rows in a grid, or write your own SQL query to look at exactly the data you want. Click a column header to sort by it, or open the stats panel to see quick numbers for that column — minimum, maximum, average, and percentiles — worked out across the whole dataset, not just the rows on screen. For editable formats (.duckdb, .parquet, .csv, .dta, .arrow/.arrows/.feather, .xlsx, .db/.sqlite), double-click a cell to change its value and save it straight back to the file; turn on Safe Mode first to keep an automatic backup and see exactly which rows changed before you commit to the edit. kdb+ tables are read directly in their real, original format — no conversion step — though they are view-only for now, since there is no way yet to write changes back into that format. Excel workbooks show one sheet per sidebar entry, and an edit rewrites just that one cell inside the workbook file, leaving the other sheets, the formulas and the cell formatting exactly as they were.

dataFileViewer.diffRowThreshold.description: Above this many rows, automatic diff-against-backup highlighting is skipped after a query — use "Diff anyway" to run it on demand instead.

dataFileViewer.maxResultRows.description: Maximum number of rows a query result sends to the view. 0 (the default) means no cap — every matching row is shown. Set a cap if very large results feel slow: sorting still runs across the whole result before the cap is applied, so the rows you see remain the true top N.

dataFileViewer.liveRefreshIntervalMs.description: Default Live refresh interval (milliseconds) used when a document has no auto-detected sheet_metadata poll-cadence hint. Also acts as a minimum spacing floor between live ticks.

dataFileViewer.previewFirstTableOnOpen.description: Preview the first table as soon as a file opens, instead of waiting for a click. For a file holding one table that click is pure ceremony; turn this off if opening a very large file should stay instant.

dataFileViewer.numberLocale.markdownDescription: Decimal convention for CSV files. `auto` samples the file and decides; a file that carries no evidence is left as text and reported, rather than guessed at — reading `1.234` the wrong way is a silent factor of 1000. `en` reads `1,234.56`; `eu` reads Turkish/European `1.234,56`. Mirrors the ETL pipeline's NUMBER_LOCALE.

dataFileViewer.chartMaxPoints.description: Most points a chart will draw. A chart plots the rows your query returns, including its LIMIT, so going over this refuses to draw and reports the real count rather than plotting a prefix that would look like a complete series.

dataFileViewer.debugLiveRefresh.description: Log Live refresh internals (stat-gate skips, watcher/timer triggers, backoff, auto-detect cache hits) to the "Data File Viewer: Live Refresh" output channel.

scripts.package: npm run build && npx vsce package
